entries.title: Critical nonpercolation on quasi-transitive graphs: exact scope
entries.statement: For independent Bernoulli bond percolation on an infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph G with p_c(G)<1, the historical Benjamini-Schramm question asks whether at p=p_c(G) there is almost surely no infinite open cluster. The p_c<1 hypothesis is essential: on the two-sided line p_c=1 and all edges are open at that parameter. This card records the precise question, not a present-day open-status verdict.
assumptions: G infinite, connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive

source.excerpt: If p_c(G)<1, then G[p_c] has no infinite clusters almost surely.

entries.title: Critical nonpercolation for quasi-transitive exponential-growth graphs
entries.statement: Hutchcroft proved in 2016 that Bernoulli bond percolation at p_c has no infinite cluster almost surely on every connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph of exponential volume growth. This is a published special class of the broader criticality question.

entries.title: Any hypothetical critical infinite component is destroyed by every independent thinning
entries.statement: Let G be countable, connected and locally finite with Bernoulli bond threshold p_c(G)>0. In the critical Bernoulli configuration, almost surely every infinite open component H, if any, has its own Bernoulli bond threshold p_c(H)=1.
entries.proof_text: For rational q in (0,1), independently retain each critically open edge with probability q. The resulting edges are iid Bernoulli(p_c q), so have no infinite component since p_c q<p_c. Conditional on the critical configuration X, the thinning restricted to each X-component has Bernoulli(q) law. For each vertex v the nonnegative conditional probability that its X-component survives this thinning has expectation zero and is therefore zero almost surely. Intersect over countably many v and rational q; monotonicity extends to every real q<1. At q=1 an infinite H survives. This is a reduction and does not exclude H.

entries.title: A critical jump appears as an atom of finite-radius Russo measures
entries.statement: Let G be infinite, connected and locally finite, let o be a vertex, and suppose 0<p_c(G)<1. Let A_n be the event that o connects inside B(o,n) to its distance-n sphere, f_n(p)=P_p(A_n), and mu_n(dp)=f_n'(p)dp on [0,p_c]. Then mu_n converges weakly to theta_o(p_c) times the point mass at p_c. In particular, pointwise control of individual pivotal edges below p_c cannot by itself rule out a critical jump.
entries.proof_text: Finite Russo differentiation gives f_n'(p)>=0 and mu_n([0,t])=f_n(t), since f_n(0)=0. For every t<p_c, f_n(t) decreases to theta_o(t)=0. The total mass f_n(p_c) decreases to theta_o(p_c). For a continuous test function h, split at p_c-delta: the lower part has vanishing mass and the upper part differs from h(p_c) times its mass by at most the modulus of continuity of h at delta. Let n tend to infinity then delta tend to zero. This is a limit theorem, not an extinction proof.

entries.title: Critical susceptibility diverges on a regular tree
entries.statement: For Bernoulli bond percolation on the D-regular tree with D>=3, p_c=1/(D-1), critical clusters are almost surely finite, but the expected critical cluster size is infinite. Thus critical extinction does not imply finite susceptibility at p_c.
entries.proof_text: The forward exploration is a Galton-Watson process with Binomial(D-1,p) offspring, so p_c=1/(D-1) and the critical process dies out almost surely. At this parameter, the sphere of radius n>=1 contains D(D-1)^(n-1) vertices, each connected to the root with probability (D-1)^(-n) along its unique path. Its expected connected-vertex count is D/(D-1) for every n, and summing over n diverges.
assumptions: Independent Bernoulli bond percolation on the infinite D-regular tree

relations.rationale: The 2016 theorem covers the exponential-growth subclass of the exact historical question.
The lemma characterizes any hypothetical infinite critical component without asserting the full question.
A positive critical survival probability appears as the limiting pivotal-measure atom.
The regular tree is an exponential-growth graph where extinction holds but critical susceptibility diverges.
